Music video

["Eyes Closed"](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=v08qmr8m_-w) on [YouTube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YouTube_video_\(identifier\) "YouTube video (identifier)")

"**Eyes Closed**" is a song by American [pop rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pop_rock "Pop rock") band [Imagine Dragons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Imagine_Dragons "Imagine Dragons"), released as the lead single off the band's sixth studio album, _[Loom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loom_\(Imagine_Dragons_album\) "Loom (Imagine Dragons album)")_ on April 3, 2024.[\[1\]](#cite_note-rolling-stone-1) The song was released through [Interscope](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interscope_Records "Interscope Records") and [Kidinakorner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kidinakorner "Kidinakorner") the same day as the music video. It was written by [Dan Reynolds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Reynolds "Dan Reynolds"), [Wayne Sermon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wayne_Sermon "Wayne Sermon"), [Ben McKee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_McKee "Ben McKee") and producers [Mattman & Robin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mattman_&_Robin "Mattman & Robin").[\[2\]](#cite_note-apple-music-2)

A remix of the song with Colombian singer [J Balvin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/J_Balvin "J Balvin") was released on May 3.[\[3\]](#cite_note-3)

## Background and themes

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Eyes_Closed_\(Imagine_Dragons_song\)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Background and themes")\]

The song has been described as a mix of [rap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rap "Rap")\-[rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_music "Rock music"), [pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pop_music "Pop music") and [alternative rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alternative_rock "Alternative rock"), with some [dubstep](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dubstep "Dubstep").[\[1\]](#cite_note-rolling-stone-1) In a statement, Reynolds said of the new track:

> After taking some time off the road and spending time catching up with family and loved ones, I finally have felt the desire to go back to the sonic places that originally brought me the most joy, but with a new outlook and mentality. The world looks much different after being a band for more than a decade. But some things will always remain the same. It’s finding that right balance of nostalgia and freshness that brings me the most joy in the studio. We had a lot of fun making this one and hope you enjoy it too.

In March 2024, "Eyes Closed" was first teased following the latest release of "[Children of the Sky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Children_of_the_Sky_\(song\) "Children of the Sky (song)") (a _[Starfield](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Starfield_\(videogame\) "Starfield (videogame)")_ song)" through various snippets, following secret codes and riddles to solve through their official website. Another snippet was released on March 27, alongside a team-based event that sorted fans into respective teams (Croyants, Reveurs, or Guerriers) based on their choices on a quick survey.[\[4\]](#cite_note-4)

The remix with [J Balvin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/J_Balvin "J Balvin") was released on May 3.[\[5\]](#cite_note-5)

"Eyes Closed" is featured on the soundtrack to [EA Sports](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/EA_Sports "EA Sports")' _[NHL 25](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NHL_25 "NHL 25")_, marking the band's third song in a soundtrack of the [_NHL_ video game series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NHL_\(video_game_series\) "NHL (video game series)").

The song appeared in the video package between [Cody Rhodes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cody_Rhodes "Cody Rhodes") and [Roman Reigns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roman_Reigns "Roman Reigns") for the Undisputed WWE Universal Championship match at [WrestleMania XL](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WrestleMania_XL "WrestleMania XL").\[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_\]

Directed by Andrew Donoho, the video follows Imagine Dragons lead singer [Dan Reynolds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Reynolds "Dan Reynolds"), who appears to wake up from death—emerging from piles of sand—in a strange world, where he encounters ancient ruins. In his journey, he encounters four doors, but he cannot seem to escape from this place, until eventually a fifth door is unveiled that he must pass through. These strange-looking ruins turn out to be a dream from his subconscious spinning a near-death experience, from the aftermath of a car crash. The video ends with Reynolds leaving the scene and walking into the street.

"**Nice To Meet You**" is a song by American [rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_music "Rock music") band [Imagine Dragons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Imagine_Dragons "Imagine Dragons") released as the second single from the band's sixth studio album [_Loom_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loom_\(Imagine_Dragons_album\) "Loom (Imagine Dragons album)"). It was released through [Interscope Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interscope_Records "Interscope Records") and [Kidinakorner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kidinakorner "Kidinakorner") on May 24, 2024.[\[3\]](#cite_note-3)

## Background and composition

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Nice_to_Meet_You_\(Imagine_Dragons_song\)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Background and composition")\]

"Nice To Meet You" was written by Imagine Dragons members [Dan Reynolds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Reynolds "Dan Reynolds"), [Wayne Sermon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wayne_Sermon "Wayne Sermon"), and [Ben McKee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_McKee "Ben McKee"), along with [Mattias Larsson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mattias_Larsson "Mattias Larsson") and [Robin Fredriksson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robin_Fredriksson "Robin Fredriksson"). It was produced by Larsson and Fredriksson and mixed by [Serban Ghenea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serban_Ghenea "Serban Ghenea") and Bryce Bordone.[\[4\]](#cite_note-4) A snippet of the song, along with snippets of "Fire in These Hills" and "[Wake Up](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wake_Up_\(Imagine_Dragons_song\) "Wake Up (Imagine Dragons song)")", were shared to the winning _Croyants_ team on the band's four doors website.[\[5\]](#cite_note-5) The band posted an official teaser of the song on May 15.[\[6\]](#cite_note-6) In an [Instagram Live](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Instagram_Live "Instagram Live"), Reynolds described the lyrics of the song:

> The song is about the dating process. I’ve always really hated that when you are dating someone, you are also kind of dating their friends. Like I didn’t sign up for that. I really like you but I really don’t have to like all your friends. The person that I wrote it about, I got her permission before getting the song out. We are friends now, but there was a moment when we were not doing good.

The official music video for "Nice To Meet You" premiered on May 24, 2024, and was directed by [Matt Eastin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matt_Eastin "Matt Eastin").[\[7\]](#cite_note-7) The video features [Dan Reynolds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Reynolds "Dan Reynolds") meeting a woman at a bar dancing to the song played by bandmates [Wayne Sermon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wayne_Sermon "Wayne Sermon") and [Ben McKee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_McKee "Ben McKee"). Eventually, the other members of the bar join in as it transforms into a 70's dance floor. After the song ends, the former two leave the bar in Reynolds' top-down car.

**Imagine Dragons** are an American [pop rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pop_rock "Pop rock") band formed in 2008, based in [Las Vegas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Las_Vegas "Las Vegas"), [Nevada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nevada "Nevada"). The band currently consists of lead singer [Dan Reynolds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Reynolds "Dan Reynolds"), guitarist [Wayne Sermon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wayne_Sermon "Wayne Sermon"), and bassist [Ben McKee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_McKee "Ben McKee").[\[1\]](#cite_note-Platzman-1)[\[2\]](#cite_note-RS-Platzman-2) Their debut single, "[It's Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/It's_Time_\(song\) "It's Time (song)")", was released in February 2012, reaching the Top 20 of various charts around the world. Their debut album, _[Night Visions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Night_Visions "Night Visions")_, which resulted in the chart-topping singles "[Radioactive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radioactive_\(Imagine_Dragons_song\) "Radioactive (Imagine Dragons song)")" and "[Demons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Demons_\(Imagine_Dragons_song\) "Demons (Imagine Dragons song)")", reached No. 2 in America on release in September 2012, and achieved Platinum sales by June 2013. _[Rolling Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling_Stone "Rolling Stone")_ named "Radioactive", which held the record for most weeks charted on the [_Billboard_ Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100"), the "biggest rock hit of the year".[\[3\]](#cite_note-imaginedragonsmusic-3)[\[4\]](#cite_note-rollingstone-4)[\[5\]](#cite_note-5)[\[6\]](#cite_note-6) [MTV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTV "MTV") called them "the year's biggest breakout band",[\[7\]](#cite_note-7) and _[Billboard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_\(magazine\) "Billboard (magazine)")_ named them their "Breakthrough Band of 2013" and "Biggest Band of 2017",[\[8\]](#cite_note-8) and placed them at the top of their "Year in Rock" rankings for 2013,[\[9\]](#cite_note-billboard.com-9) 2017,[\[10\]](#cite_note-10) and 2018.[\[11\]](#cite_note-11) Imagine Dragons topped the _Billboard_ Year-End "Top Artists – Duo/Group" category in 2018.[\[12\]](#cite_note-12)

The band's second studio album _[Smoke + Mirrors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smoke_+_Mirrors "Smoke + Mirrors")_ (2015) reached number one in the US, Canada, and the UK.[\[13\]](#cite_note-13)[\[14\]](#cite_note-14) This was followed by their third studio album _[Evolve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evolve_\(Imagine_Dragons_album\) "Evolve (Imagine Dragons album)")_ (2017), which resulted in three chart-topping singles, "[Believer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Believer_\(Imagine_Dragons_song\) "Believer (Imagine Dragons song)")", "[Thunder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thunder_\(Imagine_Dragons_song\) "Thunder (Imagine Dragons song)")", and "[Whatever It Takes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whatever_It_Takes_\(Imagine_Dragons_song\) "Whatever It Takes (Imagine Dragons song)")", also making them the artist with [the most weeks at number one on the _Billboard_ Hot Rock Songs chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_number-one_Billboard_Rock_Songs "List of number-one Billboard Rock Songs"). The album reached the top five in many countries.[\[15\]](#cite_note-15) The band's fourth studio album _[Origins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Origins_\(Imagine_Dragons_album\) "Origins (Imagine Dragons album)")_ (2018) featured the single "[Natural](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natural_\(Imagine_Dragons_song\) "Natural (Imagine Dragons song)")", which became their fifth song to top the Hot Rock Songs chart. The band has since released _[Mercury – Acts 1 & 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercury_–_Acts_1_&_2 "Mercury – Acts 1 & 2")_ (2022), a double album featuring the US top 5 hit "[Enemy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enemy_\(Imagine_Dragons_and_JID_song\) "Enemy (Imagine Dragons and JID song)")", and _[Loom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loom_\(Imagine_Dragons_album\) "Loom (Imagine Dragons album)")_ (2024), their first album without longtime drummer [Daniel Platzman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Platzman "Daniel Platzman"). Despite their popularity and commercial success, the band's music has been consistently met with mixed critical reception.

Imagine Dragons won three [American Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Music_Awards "American Music Awards"), nine [_Billboard_ Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Music_Award "Billboard Music Award"), one [Grammy Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award "Grammy Award"), one [MTV Video Music Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTV_Video_Music_Award "MTV Video Music Award"), and one [World Music Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Music_Award "World Music Award"). In May 2014, the band was nominated for 14 _Billboard_ Music Awards, including Top Artist of the Year and a Milestone Award, which recognizes innovation and creativity of artists across different genres. In April 2018, the band was nominated 11 more times for _Billboard_ Music Awards.[\[16\]](#cite_note-16)

Imagine Dragons have sold more than 74 million albums and 65 million digital songs worldwide, making them one of the [world's best-selling music artists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_best-selling_music_artists "List of best-selling music artists"). They have also earned 160 billion streams across music platforms.[\[17\]](#cite_note-:1-17) They were the most streamed group of 2018 on [Spotify](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spotify "Spotify"),[\[18\]](#cite_note-18) the first rock act to have four songs, "Radioactive", "Demons", "Believer", and "Thunder", to surpass one billion streams each,[\[19\]](#cite_note-19) and the only group in RIAA history to have four songs certified higher than Diamond.[\[20\]](#cite_note-20) According to _Billboard_, "Believer", "Thunder", and "Radioactive" were the three best performing rock songs of the 2010s.[\[21\]](#cite_note-21)

## History

### 2008–2011: Lineup changes and early EPs

In 2008, lead singer [Dan Reynolds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Reynolds "Dan Reynolds") met drummer [Andrew Tolman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_Tolman "Andrew Tolman") at [Brigham Young University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brigham_Young_University "Brigham Young University"), where they were both students.[\[22\]](#cite_note-22) Reynolds and Tolman recruited [Andrew Beck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_Beck_\(musician\) "Andrew Beck (musician)"), Dave Lemke, and Aurora Florence to play guitar, bass, and piano, respectively, for their band. Their name is an [anagram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anagram "Anagram") for a phrase only known to members of the group, which Reynolds stated each member approved of.[\[23\]](#cite_note-23) The five-piece recorded demos that they uploaded to MySpace that year, but Beck and Florence left the band later that year. In 2009, Tolman recruited long-time high school friend [Wayne Sermon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Wayne_Sermon "Daniel Wayne Sermon"), who had graduated from [Berklee College of Music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berklee_College_of_Music "Berklee College of Music"), to play guitar. Tolman later recruited his wife, Brittany Tolman, to sing back-up and play keys, and the band began to play shows together again. Lemke left the band shortly thereafter, leading Sermon to recruit another Berklee music student, [Ben McKee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_McKee "Ben McKee"), to join the band as their bassist and complete the line-up.[\[24\]](#cite_note-24)[\[25\]](#cite_note-25) The band garnered a large following in their hometown of [Provo, Utah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Provo,_Utah "Provo, Utah"),[\[26\]](#cite_note-26)[\[27\]](#cite_note-27) before the members moved to [Las Vegas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Las_Vegas "Las Vegas"), the hometown of Dan Reynolds, where the band recorded and released their first three EPs.[\[28\]](#cite_note-28)

The band released a self-titled EP _[Imagine Dragons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Imagine_Dragons_\(EP\) "Imagine Dragons (EP)")_ on September 1, 2009, and _[Hell and Silence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hell_and_Silence "Hell and Silence")_ on March 10, 2010, both recorded at [Battle Born Studios](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_Born_Studios "Battle Born Studios"), in Las Vegas.[\[29\]](#cite_note-lasvegasweekly1-29)[\[30\]](#cite_note-30)[\[31\]](#cite_note-31) Six months after releasing their third EP, _[It's Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/It's_Time_\(EP\) "It's Time (EP)")_, on March 12, 2011, they signed a record deal with Interscope Records on November 18, 2011.[\[32\]](#cite_note-32)

They got their first big break when [Train](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Train_\(band\) "Train (band)")'s frontman [Pat Monahan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pat_Monahan "Pat Monahan") fell sick just prior to the Bite of Las Vegas Festival 2009. Imagine Dragons were called to fill in and performed to a crowd of more than 26,000 people.[\[33\]](#cite_note-33) Local accolades including "Best CD of 2011" (_Vegas SEVEN_),[\[34\]](#cite_note-34) "Best Local Indie Band 2010" (_[Las Vegas Weekly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Las_Vegas_Weekly "Las Vegas Weekly")_),[\[35\]](#cite_note-35) "Las Vegas' Newest Must See Live Act" (_[Las Vegas CityLife](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Las_Vegas_CityLife "Las Vegas CityLife")_),[\[36\]](#cite_note-lasvegascitylife1-36)\[_[new archival link needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Archiving_a_source "Help:Archiving a source")_\] Vegas Music Summit Headliner 2010,[\[37\]](#cite_note-37) and more sent the band on a positive trajectory. In November 2011, they signed with [Interscope Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interscope_Records "Interscope Records") and began working with English Grammy Award-winning producer [Alex da Kid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alex_da_Kid "Alex da Kid").[\[38\]](#cite_note-38) Eventually, the Tolmans left the group. Drummer [Daniel Platzman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Platzman "Daniel Platzman") and keyboardist [Theresa Flaminio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DANiiVORY "DANiiVORY") were recruited by McKee in August 2011, prior to the band's label deal in November 2011.[\[39\]](#cite_note-39) Flaminio departed from the group around the time of the band's deal with Interscope, leaving the band a four-piece.

### 2012–2014: _Night Visions_

The band worked closely with Alex da Kid, with whom they recorded their first major-label release at [Westlake Recording Studios](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Westlake_Recording_Studios "Westlake Recording Studios") in [West Hollywood, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Hollywood,_California "West Hollywood, California").

An EP entitled _[Continued Silence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Continued_Silence "Continued Silence")_ was released on February 14, 2012 digitally and peaked at number 40 on the [_Billboard_ 200](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_200 "Billboard 200"). The band also released an EP titled _[Hear Me](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hear_Me_\(EP\) "Hear Me (EP)")_ in 2012.

Shortly after, "[It's Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/It's_Time_\(Imagine_Dragons_song\) "It's Time (Imagine Dragons song)")" was released as a single and peaked at number 15 on the [_Billboard_ Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100").[\[40\]](#cite_note-40) The music video debuted on April 17, 2012, on all [MTV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTV "MTV") affiliates and was subsequently nominated for an [MTV Video Music Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTV_Video_Music_Award "MTV Video Music Award") in the "Best Rock Video" category.[\[41\]](#cite_note-41) "It's Time" was certified a 7× platinum single by the [RIAA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Recording_Industry_Association_of_America "Recording Industry Association of America").[\[42\]](#cite_note-music.yahoo.com-42)

The band finished recording their debut album _[Night Visions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Night_Visions "Night Visions")_ in the summer of 2012 at [Studio X](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Studio_at_the_Palms "Studio at the Palms") inside [Palms Casino Resort](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palms_Casino_Resort "Palms Casino Resort") and released the album in the United States on September 4, 2012. It peaked at No. 2 on the Billboard 200 chart with first week sales in excess of 83,000 copies, the highest charting for a debut rock album since 2006.[\[43\]](#cite_note-43) The album also reached No. 1 on the Billboard [Alternative](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Top_Alternative_Albums "Top Alternative Albums") and [Rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Top_Rock_Albums "Top Rock Albums") Album charts as well as the top ten on the Australian, Austrian, Canadian, Dutch, German, Irish, Norwegian, Portuguese, Scottish, Spanish, and United Kingdom Albums charts. It won a [Billboard Music Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Music_Award "Billboard Music Award") for Top Rock Album and was nominated for the [Juno Award for International Album of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juno_Award_for_International_Album_of_the_Year "Juno Award for International Album of the Year").[\[44\]](#cite_note-44) _Night Visions_ is certified platinum in the US by the RIAA as well as in Australia, Austria, Brazil, Canada, Mexico, New Zealand, Poland, Portugal, Sweden, Switzerland, and the UK. The album produced three tracks that reached the [_Billboard_ Top 40](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100"), four tracks in the [ARIA Top 40](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ARIA_Charts "ARIA Charts"), and five tracks charting in the [UK Top 40](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UK_Singles_Chart "UK Singles Chart").

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7e/Imagine_Dragons_-_Ilosaarirock_2013_2.jpg/250px-Imagine_Dragons_-_Ilosaarirock_2013_2.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Imagine_Dragons_-_Ilosaarirock_2013_2.jpg)

The band embarked on the Night Visions Tour in 2013.

The album's second single "[Radioactive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radioactive_\(Imagine_Dragons_song\) "Radioactive (Imagine Dragons song)")" reached No. 1 on the _Billboard_ Alternative Songs, _Billboard_ Rock Songs, and Swedish singles chart and has sold more than 14 million singles in the United States, entering the top 3 of the most selling songs digitally ever.[\[45\]](#cite_note-Gold_&_Platinum-45) It also smashed the record of the longest running song on the _Billboard_ Hot 100 by spending 87 weeks before being broken by [The Weeknd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Weeknd "The Weeknd")'s "[Blinding Lights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blinding_Lights "Blinding Lights")" in 2021.[\[46\]](#cite_note-46) "Radioactive" stayed at No. 1 on the Hot Rock Songs chart for a record-breaking 23 weeks and ultimately became the genre's biggest hit of 2013.[\[47\]](#cite_note-47) It peaked at No. 3, becoming their first top ten single in the United States and broke the record for the longest run into the top five. It is the best-selling rock song on the Nielsen SoundScan running list of best-selling rock songs in digital history.[\[48\]](#cite_note-48) By the end of 2013, "Radioactive" had already sold over three million copies.[\[49\]](#cite_note-49) _[Rolling Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling_Stone "Rolling Stone")_ called it "the biggest rock hit of the year". It was also the most streamed song of 2013 on [Spotify](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spotify "Spotify") in the United States.[\[50\]](#cite_note-usatoday.com-50) It was nominated for the [Grammy Award for Record of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Record_of_the_Year "Grammy Award for Record of the Year") and the [Grammy Award for Best Rock Performance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_Rock_Performance "Grammy Award for Best Rock Performance") at the [56th Annual Grammy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/56th_Annual_Grammy_Awards "56th Annual Grammy Awards"), winning the latter of the two. The band performed a medley of "Radioactive" and "[M.A.A.D City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M.A.A.D_City "M.A.A.D City")" alongside rapper [Kendrick Lamar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kendrick_Lamar "Kendrick Lamar") at the ceremony. A remixed version of "Radioactive", featuring a newly added verse from Lamar, was released the next day and performed on the February 1, 2014 episode of _[Saturday Night Live](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saturday_Night_Live "Saturday Night Live")_.

Third single "[Demons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Demons_\(Imagine_Dragons_song\) "Demons (Imagine Dragons song)")" reached No. 1 on the _Billboard_ Pop Songs, peaked at No. 6 on the _Billboard_ [Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100") and spent 61 weeks on it.[\[42\]](#cite_note-music.yahoo.com-42)[\[51\]](#cite_note-51) In 2021, RIAA declared that the song has become the band's third diamond selling song in the US. Fourth single "[On Top Of The World](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/On_Top_of_the_World_\(Imagine_Dragons_song\) "On Top of the World (Imagine Dragons song)")" reached a peak of No. 79 on the [Billboard Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100") and also spent 20 weeks on the chart. In the US, the non-singles off the album, "Bleeding Out" and "Amsterdam" were certified platinum while "Hear Me" and "Tiptoe" were certified gold.[\[45\]](#cite_note-Gold_&_Platinum-45) _[Billboard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_\(magazine\) "Billboard (magazine)")_ listed them as one of "2012's Brightest New Stars" and later "The Breakout Band of 2013".[\[52\]](#cite_note-52) Imagine Dragons won the 2014 [Billboard Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Music_Awards "Billboard Music Awards") for Top Duo/Group, Top Hot 100 Artist, and Top Rock Artist. Amazon.com called the band their "Favorite Rock Artist of 2012".[\[53\]](#cite_note-53)

In 2013, Imagine Dragons returned to Europe and North America with the Night Visions Tour.[\[54\]](#cite_note-54) The band announced 13 additional US summer tour dates which also sold out.[\[55\]](#cite_note-55) The band then announced a North America Amphitheatre tour.[\[56\]](#cite_note-56) [Pollstar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pollstar "Pollstar") listed the band in their Top 20 Concert Tours list by average box office gross despite their average ticket price being the third lowest on the list.[\[57\]](#cite_note-57)\[_[new archival link needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Archiving_a_source "Help:Archiving a source")_\] The band released a live album, _[Live at Independent Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_at_Independent_Records "Live at Independent Records")_, in April 2013.[\[58\]](#cite_note-livedragons-58)

### 2014–2016: _Smoke + Mirrors_

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d2/Imagine_Dragons_July_6_2015_Verizon_Center.jpg/250px-Imagine_Dragons_July_6_2015_Verizon_Center.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Imagine_Dragons_July_6_2015_Verizon_Center.jpg)

Imagine Dragons at [Verizon Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Capital_One_Arena "Capital One Arena"), Washington, D.C., on the _Smoke + Mirrors_ tour in July 2015

The idea behind the second studio album, dubbed as their "[New Year's resolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Year's_resolution "New Year's resolution")",[\[59\]](#cite_note-59) was to create music and finish it when the band feels that their work is done.[\[60\]](#cite_note-60) Since the beginning of the Night Visions Tour, the band had been writing new material for an upcoming album, and, even as early as the start of the tour, had been recording [demos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Demo_\(music\) "Demo (music)") for the album, before entering the studio.[\[61\]](#cite_note-61) By the time that they entered the studio to work on the album, they had amassed 50 demos to work from.[\[62\]](#cite_note-rollingstonegrammy-62)

Prior to the album's release, Imagine Dragons released a number of singles for other projects including a song for the film _[Transformers: Age of Extinction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Age_of_Extinction "Transformers: Age of Extinction")_, called "[Battle Cry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_Cry_\(Imagine_Dragons_song\) "Battle Cry (Imagine Dragons song)")" in June, 2014 and the song "[Warriors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warriors_\(Imagine_Dragons_song\) "Warriors (Imagine Dragons song)")" for the [2014 _League of Legends_ World Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Season_4_World_Championship "Season 4 World Championship") in September, 2014.[\[63\]](#cite_note-63)

On October 24, they revealed the lead single to the upcoming album, "[I Bet My Life](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Bet_My_Life_\(Imagine_Dragons_song\) "I Bet My Life (Imagine Dragons song)")" via several visual snippets on Facebook and Instagram. It was released on October 27.[\[64\]](#cite_note-64) It was sent to US Alternative radio for ads on November 3.[\[65\]](#cite_note-65) On December 16, the band announced their second album _[Smoke + Mirrors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smoke_+_Mirrors "Smoke + Mirrors")_, along with the release of its second single "[Gold](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gold_\(Imagine_Dragons_song\) "Gold (Imagine Dragons song)")".[\[66\]](#cite_note-66) "[Shots](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shots_\(Imagine_Dragons_song\) "Shots (Imagine Dragons song)")" was released as the album's third single on January 26, 2015.[\[67\]](#cite_note-67)

Imagine Dragons played at the [Mayan Theater](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mayan_Theater "Mayan Theater") in [Los Angeles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles "Los Angeles") on February 5, 2015. The half-hour set included the live debut of unreleased songs "Summer" and "[I'm So Sorry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I'm_So_Sorry "I'm So Sorry")".[\[68\]](#cite_note-68) On February 8, the band partnered with [Target](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Target_Corporation "Target Corporation") for a performance of "Shots" as part of a live commercial aired during the [Grammy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/57th_Annual_Grammy_Awards "57th Annual Grammy Awards"). _Smoke + Mirrors_ was released on February 17. The album debuted atop the Billboard 200, making it the band's first number one album. The band began a world tour in support of the album on June 3 in [Portland, Oregon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portland,_Oregon "Portland, Oregon").

During the band's tour, Imagine Dragons released two non-album singles. "[Roots](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roots_\(Imagine_Dragons_song\) "Roots (Imagine Dragons song)")" was released on August 26, 2015, and "[I Was Me](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Was_Me "I Was Me")" on October 12, 2015, via [iTunes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ITunes "ITunes"). The band also released a cover of "I Love You All the Time" by [Eagles of Death Metal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eagles_of_Death_Metal "Eagles of Death Metal") on December 18, 2015, in support of the victims of the [November 2015 Paris attacks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/November_2015_Paris_attacks "November 2015 Paris attacks"). The [Smoke + Mirrors Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smoke_+_Mirrors_Tour "Smoke + Mirrors Tour") ended on February 5, 2016, in [Amsterdam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amsterdam "Amsterdam"). The band released a one night only [concert film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Concert_film "Concert film"), _Imagine Dragons In Concert: Smoke + Mirrors_, in select theaters on March 2, 2016, which was later released on DVD and Blu-Ray.[\[69\]](#cite_note-69)

Following the tour, the band planned to take a hiatus. They released the soundtracks songs "[Not Today](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Today_\(Imagine_Dragons_song\) "Not Today (Imagine Dragons song)")" from _[Me Before You](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Me_Before_You_\(soundtrack\) "Me Before You (soundtrack)")_ and "[Sucker for Pain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sucker_for_Pain "Sucker for Pain")" from _[Suicide Squad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suicide_Squad_\(soundtrack\) "Suicide Squad (soundtrack)")_ with [Lil Wayne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Wayne "Lil Wayne"), [Wiz Khalifa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wiz_Khalifa "Wiz Khalifa"), [Logic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Logic_\(rapper\) "Logic (rapper)"), [Ty Dolla Sign](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ty_Dolla_Sign "Ty Dolla Sign"), and [X Ambassadors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/X_Ambassadors "X Ambassadors") in April and June, respectively.[\[70\]](#cite_note-70)[\[71\]](#cite_note-71)

### 2016–2020: _Evolve_ and _Origins_

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/23/Imagine_Dragons_-_Uncasville_CT_-_November_2017_-_1.jpg/250px-Imagine_Dragons_-_Uncasville_CT_-_November_2017_-_1.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Imagine_Dragons_-_Uncasville_CT_-_November_2017_-_1.jpg)

Imagine Dragons performing at [Mohegan Sun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mohegan_Sun "Mohegan Sun") during the Evolve tour in November 2017.

Imagine Dragons began recording their third studio album in September 2016. The band teased the upcoming album by posting cryptic messages on their Twitter account for the next four months. They released the song "[Levitate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Levitate_\(Imagine_Dragons_song\) "Levitate (Imagine Dragons song)")", recorded for the film _[Passengers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Passengers_\(2016_film\) "Passengers (2016 film)")_, on December 2, 2016. On January 28, 2017, the band started posting a series of videos teasing the album's first single.[\[72\]](#cite_note-72) The time-lapse videos featured lead singer Dan Reynolds drawing surreal images on a drawing pad. [Morse code](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morse_code "Morse code") was hidden in the videos and translated to "objects of same color".\[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_\]

On February 1, 2017, Imagine Dragons released "[Believer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Believer_\(Imagine_Dragons_song\) "Believer (Imagine Dragons song)")" as the lead single for their next album. "Believer" was used as part of a [Super Bowl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl "Super Bowl") ad for the [Nintendo Switch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nintendo_Switch "Nintendo Switch").[\[73\]](#cite_note-73) On April

# Imagine Dragons

This article is about the band. For their self-titled EP, see [_Imagine Dragons_ (EP)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Imagine_Dragons_\(EP\) "Imagine Dragons (EP)").

Imagine Dragons

[![Imagine Dragons at Mohegan Sun in 2017. Left to right: Wayne Sermon, Dan Reynolds, former drummer Daniel Platzman, and Ben McKee.](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a2/Imagine_Dragons_-_Uncasville_CT_-_November_2017_-_2.jpg/330px-Imagine_Dragons_-_Uncasville_CT_-_November_2017_-_2.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Imagine_Dragons_-_Uncasville_CT_-_November_2017_-_2.jpg "Imagine Dragons at Mohegan Sun in 2017. Left to right: Wayne Sermon, Dan Reynolds, former drummer Daniel Platzman, and Ben McKee.")

Imagine Dragons at Mohegan Sun in 2017. Left to right: [Wayne Sermon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wayne_Sermon "Wayne Sermon"), [Dan Reynolds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Reynolds "Dan Reynolds"), former drummer [Daniel Platzman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Platzman "Daniel Platzman"), and [Ben McKee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_McKee "Ben McKee").

Background information

Genres

*   [Daniel Platzman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Platzman "Daniel Platzman")

**Imagine Dragons** are an American [pop rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pop_rock "Pop rock") band formed in 2008, based in [Las Vegas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Las_Vegas "Las Vegas"), [Nevada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nevada "Nevada"). The band currently consists of lead singer [Dan Reynolds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Reynolds "Dan Reynolds"), guitarist [Wayne Sermon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wayne_Sermon "Wayne Sermon"), and bassist [Ben McKee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_McKee "Ben McKee").[\[1\]](#cite_note-Platzman-1)[\[2\]](#cite_note-RS-Platzman-2) Their debut single, "[It's Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/It's_Time_\(song\) "It's Time (song)")", was released in February 2012, reaching the Top 20 of various charts around the world. Their debut album, _[Night Visions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Night_Visions "Night Visions")_, which resulted in the chart-topping singles "[Radioactive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radioactive_\(Imagine_Dragons_song\) "Radioactive (Imagine Dragons song)")" and "[Demons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Demons_\(Imagine_Dragons_song\) "Demons (Imagine Dragons song)")", reached No. 2 in America on release in September 2012, and achieved Platinum sales by June 2013. _[Rolling Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling_Stone "Rolling Stone")_ named "Radioactive", which held the record for most weeks charted on the [_Billboard_ Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100"), the "biggest rock hit of the year".[\[3\]](#cite_note-imaginedragonsmusic-3)[\[4\]](#cite_note-rollingstone-4)[\[5\]](#cite_note-5)[\[6\]](#cite_note-6) [MTV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTV "MTV") called them "the year's biggest breakout band",[\[7\]](#cite_note-7) and _[Billboard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_\(magazine\) "Billboard (magazine)")_ named them their "Breakthrough Band of 2013" and "Biggest Band of 2017",[\[8\]](#cite_note-8) and placed them at the top of their "Year in Rock" rankings for 2013,[\[9\]](#cite_note-billboard.com-9) 2017,[\[10\]](#cite_note-10) and 2018.[\[11\]](#cite_note-11) Imagine Dragons topped the _Billboard_ Year-End "Top Artists – Duo/Group" category in 2018.[\[12\]](#cite_note-12)

The band's second studio album _[Smoke + Mirrors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smoke_+_Mirrors "Smoke + Mirrors")_ (2015) reached number one in the US, Canada, and the UK.[\[13\]](#cite_note-13)[\[14\]](#cite_note-14) This was followed by their third studio album _[Evolve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evolve_\(Imagine_Dragons_album\) "Evolve (Imagine Dragons album)")_ (2017), which resulted in three chart-topping singles, "[Believer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Believer_\(Imagine_Dragons_song\) "Believer (Imagine Dragons song)")", "[Thunder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thunder_\(Imagine_Dragons_song\) "Thunder (Imagine Dragons song)")", and "[Whatever It Takes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whatever_It_Takes_\(Imagine_Dragons_song\) "Whatever It Takes (Imagine Dragons song)")", also making them the artist with [the most weeks at number one on the _Billboard_ Hot Rock Songs chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_number-one_Billboard_Rock_Songs "List of number-one Billboard Rock Songs"). The album reached the top five in many countries.[\[15\]](#cite_note-15) The band's fourth studio album _[Origins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Origins_\(Imagine_Dragons_album\) "Origins (Imagine Dragons album)")_ (2018) featured the single "[Natural](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natural_\(Imagine_Dragons_song\) "Natural (Imagine Dragons song)")", which became their fifth song to top the Hot Rock Songs chart. The band has since released _[Mercury – Acts 1 & 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercury_–_Acts_1_&_2 "Mercury – Acts 1 & 2")_ (2022), a double album featuring the US top 5 hit "[Enemy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enemy_\(Imagine_Dragons_and_JID_song\) "Enemy (Imagine Dragons and JID song)")", and _[Loom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loom_\(Imagine_Dragons_album\) "Loom (Imagine Dragons album)")_ (2024), their first album without longtime drummer [Daniel Platzman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Platzman "Daniel Platzman"). Despite their popularity and commercial success, the band's music has been consistently met with mixed critical reception.

Imagine Dragons won three [American Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Music_Awards "American Music Awards"), nine [_Billboard_ Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Music_Award "Billboard Music Award"), one [Grammy Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award "Grammy Award"), one [MTV Video Music Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTV_Video_Music_Award "MTV Video Music Award"), and one [World Music Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Music_Award "World Music Award"). In May 2014, the band was nominated for 14 _Billboard_ Music Awards, including Top Artist of the Year and a Milestone Award, which recognizes innovation and creativity of artists across different genres. In April 2018, the band was nominated 11 more times for _Billboard_ Music Awards.[\[16\]](#cite_note-16)

Imagine Dragons have sold more than 74 million albums and 65 million digital songs worldwide, making them one of the [world's best-selling music artists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_best-selling_music_artists "List of best-selling music artists"). They have also earned 160 billion streams across music platforms.[\[17\]](#cite_note-:1-17) They were the most streamed group of 2018 on [Spotify](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spotify "Spotify"),[\[18\]](#cite_note-18) the first rock act to have four songs, "Radioactive", "Demons", "Believer", and "Thunder", to surpass one billion streams each,[\[19\]](#cite_note-19) and the only group in RIAA history to have four songs certified higher than Diamond.[\[20\]](#cite_note-20) According to _Billboard_, "Believer", "Thunder", and "Radioactive" were the three best performing rock songs of the 2010s.[\[21\]](#cite_note-21)

## History

### 2008–2011: Lineup changes and early EPs

In 2008, lead singer [Dan Reynolds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Reynolds "Dan Reynolds") met drummer [Andrew Tolman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_Tolman "Andrew Tolman") at [Brigham Young University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brigham_Young_University "Brigham Young University"), where they were both students.[\[22\]](#cite_note-22) Reynolds and Tolman recruited [Andrew Beck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_Beck_\(musician\) "Andrew Beck (musician)"), Dave Lemke, and Aurora Florence to play guitar, bass, and piano, respectively, for their band. Their name is an [anagram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anagram "Anagram") for a phrase only known to members of the group, which Reynolds stated each member approved of.[\[23\]](#cite_note-23) The five-piece recorded demos that they uploaded to MySpace that year, but Beck and Florence left the band later that year. In 2009, Tolman recruited long-time high school friend [Wayne Sermon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Wayne_Sermon "Daniel Wayne Sermon"), who had graduated from [Berklee College of Music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berklee_College_of_Music "Berklee College of Music"), to play guitar. Tolman later recruited his wife, Brittany Tolman, to sing back-up and play keys, and the band began to play shows together again. Lemke left the band shortly thereafter, leading Sermon to recruit another Berklee music student, [Ben McKee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_McKee "Ben McKee"), to join the band as their bassist and complete the line-up.[\[24\]](#cite_note-24)[\[25\]](#cite_note-25) The band garnered a large following in their hometown of [Provo, Utah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Provo,_Utah "Provo, Utah"),[\[26\]](#cite_note-26)[\[27\]](#cite_note-27) before the members moved to [Las Vegas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Las_Vegas "Las Vegas"), the hometown of Dan Reynolds, where the band recorded and released their first three EPs.[\[28\]](#cite_note-28)

The band released a self-titled EP _[Imagine Dragons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Imagine_Dragons_\(EP\) "Imagine Dragons (EP)")_ on September 1, 2009, and _[Hell and Silence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hell_and_Silence "Hell and Silence")_ on March 10, 2010, both recorded at [Battle Born Studios](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_Born_Studios "Battle Born Studios"), in Las Vegas.[\[29\]](#cite_note-lasvegasweekly1-29)[\[30\]](#cite_note-30)[\[31\]](#cite_note-31) Six months after releasing their third EP, _[It's Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/It's_Time_\(EP\) "It's Time (EP)")_, on March 12, 2011, they signed a record deal with Interscope Records on November 18, 2011.[\[32\]](#cite_note-32)

They got their first big break when [Train](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Train_\(band\) "Train (band)")'s frontman [Pat Monahan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pat_Monahan "Pat Monahan") fell sick just prior to the Bite of Las Vegas Festival 2009. Imagine Dragons were called to fill in and performed to a crowd of more than 26,000 people.[\[33\]](#cite_note-33) Local accolades including "Best CD of 2011" (_Vegas SEVEN_),[\[34\]](#cite_note-34) "Best Local Indie Band 2010" (_[Las Vegas Weekly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Las_Vegas_Weekly "Las Vegas Weekly")_),[\[35\]](#cite_note-35) "Las Vegas' Newest Must See Live Act" (_[Las Vegas CityLife](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Las_Vegas_CityLife "Las Vegas CityLife")_),[\[36\]](#cite_note-lasvegascitylife1-36)\[_[new archival link needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Archiving_a_source "Help:Archiving a source")_\] Vegas Music Summit Headliner 2010,[\[37\]](#cite_note-37) and more sent the band on a positive trajectory. In November 2011, they signed with [Interscope Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interscope_Records "Interscope Records") and began working with English Grammy Award-winning producer [Alex da Kid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alex_da_Kid "Alex da Kid").[\[38\]](#cite_note-38) Eventually, the Tolmans left the group. Drummer [Daniel Platzman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Platzman "Daniel Platzman") and keyboardist [Theresa Flaminio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DANiiVORY "DANiiVORY") were recruited by McKee in August 2011, prior to the band's label deal in November 2011.[\[39\]](#cite_note-39) Flaminio departed from the group around the time of the band's deal with Interscope, leaving the band a four-piece.

### 2012–2014: _Night Visions_

The band worked closely with Alex da Kid, with whom they recorded their first major-label release at [Westlake Recording Studios](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Westlake_Recording_Studios "Westlake Recording Studios") in [West Hollywood, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Hollywood,_California "West Hollywood, California").

An EP entitled _[Continued Silence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Continued_Silence "Continued Silence")_ was released on February 14, 2012 digitally and peaked at number 40 on the [_Billboard_ 200](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_200 "Billboard 200"). The band also released an EP titled _[Hear Me](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hear_Me_\(EP\) "Hear Me (EP)")_ in 2012.

Shortly after, "[It's Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/It's_Time_\(Imagine_Dragons_song\) "It's Time (Imagine Dragons song)")" was released as a single and peaked at number 15 on the [_Billboard_ Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100").[\[40\]](#cite_note-40) The music video debuted on April 17, 2012, on all [MTV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTV "MTV") affiliates and was subsequently nominated for an [MTV Video Music Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTV_Video_Music_Award "MTV Video Music Award") in the "Best Rock Video" category.[\[41\]](#cite_note-41) "It's Time" was certified a 7× platinum single by the [RIAA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Recording_Industry_Association_of_America "Recording Industry Association of America").[\[42\]](#cite_note-music.yahoo.com-42)

The band finished recording their debut album _[Night Visions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Night_Visions "Night Visions")_ in the summer of 2012 at [Studio X](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Studio_at_the_Palms "Studio at the Palms") inside [Palms Casino Resort](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palms_Casino_Resort "Palms Casino Resort") and released the album in the United States on September 4, 2012. It peaked at No. 2 on the Billboard 200 chart with first week sales in excess of 83,000 copies, the highest charting for a debut rock album since 2006.[\[43\]](#cite_note-43) The album also reached No. 1 on the Billboard [Alternative](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Top_Alternative_Albums "Top Alternative Albums") and [Rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Top_Rock_Albums "Top Rock Albums") Album charts as well as the top ten on the Australian, Austrian, Canadian, Dutch, German, Irish, Norwegian, Portuguese, Scottish, Spanish, and United Kingdom Albums charts. It won a [Billboard Music Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Music_Award "Billboard Music Award") for Top Rock Album and was nominated for the [Juno Award for International Album of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juno_Award_for_International_Album_of_the_Year "Juno Award for International Album of the Year").[\[44\]](#cite_note-44) _Night Visions_ is certified platinum in the US by the RIAA as well as in Australia, Austria, Brazil, Canada, Mexico, New Zealand, Poland, Portugal, Sweden, Switzerland, and the UK. The album produced three tracks that reached the [_Billboard_ Top 40](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100"), four tracks in the [ARIA Top 40](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ARIA_Charts "ARIA Charts"), and five tracks charting in the [UK Top 40](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UK_Singles_Chart "UK Singles Chart").

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7e/Imagine_Dragons_-_Ilosaarirock_2013_2.jpg/250px-Imagine_Dragons_-_Ilosaarirock_2013_2.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Imagine_Dragons_-_Ilosaarirock_2013_2.jpg)

The band embarked on the Night Visions Tour in 2013.

The album's second single "[Radioactive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radioactive_\(Imagine_Dragons_song\) "Radioactive (Imagine Dragons song)")" reached No. 1 on the _Billboard_ Alternative Songs, _Billboard_ Rock Songs, and Swedish singles chart and has sold more than 14 million singles in the United States, entering the top 3 of the most selling songs digitally ever.[\[45\]](#cite_note-Gold_&_Platinum-45) It also smashed the record of the longest running song on the _Billboard_ Hot 100 by spending 87 weeks before being broken by [The Weeknd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Weeknd "The Weeknd")'s "[Blinding Lights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blinding_Lights "Blinding Lights")" in 2021.[\[46\]](#cite_note-46) "Radioactive" stayed at No. 1 on the Hot Rock Songs chart for a record-breaking 23 weeks and ultimately became the genre's biggest hit of 2013.[\[47\]](#cite_note-47) It peaked at No. 3, becoming their first top ten single in the United States and broke the record for the longest run into the top five. It is the best-selling rock song on the Nielsen SoundScan running list of best-selling rock songs in digital history.[\[48\]](#cite_note-48) By the end of 2013, "Radioactive" had already sold over three million copies.[\[49\]](#cite_note-49) _[Rolling Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling_Stone "Rolling Stone")_ called it "the biggest rock hit of the year". It was also the most streamed song of 2013 on [Spotify](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spotify "Spotify") in the United States.[\[50\]](#cite_note-usatoday.com-50) It was nominated for the [Grammy Award for Record of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Record_of_the_Year "Grammy Award for Record of the Year") and the [Grammy Award for Best Rock Performance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_Rock_Performance "Grammy Award for Best Rock Performance") at the [56th Annual Grammy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/56th_Annual_Grammy_Awards "56th Annual Grammy Awards"), winning the latter of the two. The band performed a medley of "Radioactive" and "[M.A.A.D City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M.A.A.D_City "M.A.A.D City")" alongside rapper [Kendrick Lamar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kendrick_Lamar "Kendrick Lamar") at the ceremony. A remixed version of "Radioactive", featuring a newly added verse from Lamar, was released the next day and performed on the February 1, 2014 episode of _[Saturday Night Live](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saturday_Night_Live "Saturday Night Live")_.

Third single "[Demons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Demons_\(Imagine_Dragons_song\) "Demons (Imagine Dragons song)")" reached No. 1 on the _Billboard_ Pop Songs, peaked at No. 6 on the _Billboard_ [Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100") and spent 61 weeks on it.[\[42\]](#cite_note-music.yahoo.com-42)[\[51\]](#cite_note-51) In 2021, RIAA declared that the song has become the band's third diamond selling song in the US. Fourth single "[On Top Of The World](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/On_Top_of_the_World_\(Imagine_Dragons_song\) "On Top of the World (Imagine Dragons song)")" reached a peak of No. 79 on the [Billboard Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100") and also spent 20 weeks on the chart. In the US, the non-singles off the album, "Bleeding Out" and "Amsterdam" were certified platinum while "Hear Me" and "Tiptoe" were certified gold.[\[45\]](#cite_note-Gold_&_Platinum-45) _[Billboard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_\(magazine\) "Billboard (magazine)")_ listed them as one of "2012's Brightest New Stars" and later "The Breakout Band of 2013".[\[52\]](#cite_note-52) Imagine Dragons won the 2014 [Billboard Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Music_Awards "Billboard Music Awards") for Top Duo/Group, Top Hot 100 Artist, and Top Rock Artist. Amazon.com called the band their "Favorite Rock Artist of 2012".[\[53\]](#cite_note-53)

In 2013, Imagine Dragons returned to Europe and North America with the Night Visions Tour.[\[54\]](#cite_note-54) The band announced 13 additional US summer tour dates which also sold out.[\[55\]](#cite_note-55) The band then announced a North America Amphitheatre tour.[\[56\]](#cite_note-56) [Pollstar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pollstar "Pollstar") listed the band in their Top 20 Concert Tours list by average box office gross despite their average ticket price being the third lowest on the list.[\[57\]](#cite_note-57)\[_[new archival link needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Archiving_a_source "Help:Archiving a source")_\] The band released a live album, _[Live at Independent Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_at_Independent_Records "Live at Independent Records")_, in April 2013.[\[58\]](#cite_note-livedragons-58)

### 2014–2016: _Smoke + Mirrors_

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d2/Imagine_Dragons_July_6_2015_Verizon_Center.jpg/250px-Imagine_Dragons_July_6_2015_Verizon_Center.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Imagine_Dragons_July_6_2015_Verizon_Center.jpg)

Imagine Dragons at [Verizon Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Capital_One_Arena "Capital One Arena"), Washington, D.C., on the _Smoke + Mirrors_ tour in July 2015

The idea behind the second studio album, dubbed as their "[New Year's resolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Year's_resolution "New Year's resolution")",[\[59\]](#cite_note-59) was to create music and finish it when the band feels that their work is done.[\[60\]](#cite_note-60) Since the beginning of the Night Visions Tour, the band had been writing new material for an upcoming album, and, even as early as the start of the tour, had been recording [demos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Demo_\(music\) "Demo (music)") for the album, before entering the studio.[\[61\]](#cite_note-61) By the time that they entered the studio to work on the album, they had amassed 50 demos to work from.[\[62\]](#cite_note-rollingstonegrammy-62)

Prior to the album's release, Imagine Dragons released a number of singles for other projects including a song for the film _[Transformers: Age of Extinction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformers:_Age_of_Extinction "Transformers: Age of Extinction")_, called "[Battle Cry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_Cry_\(Imagine_Dragons_song\) "Battle Cry (Imagine Dragons song)")" in June, 2014 and the song "[Warriors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warriors_\(Imagine_Dragons_song\) "Warriors (Imagine Dragons song)")" for the [2014 _League of Legends_ World Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Season_4_World_Championship "Season 4 World Championship") in September, 2014.[\[63\]](#cite_note-63)

On October 24, they revealed the lead single to the upcoming album, "[I Bet My Life](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Bet_My_Life_\(Imagine_Dragons_song\) "I Bet My Life (Imagine Dragons song)")" via several visual snippets on Facebook and Instagram. It was released on October 27.[\[64\]](#cite_note-64) It was sent to US Alternative radio for ads on November 3.[\[65\]](#cite_note-65) On December 16, the band announced their second album _[Smoke + Mirrors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smoke_+_Mirrors "Smoke + Mirrors")_, along with the release of its second single "[Gold](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gold_\(Imagine_Dragons_song\) "Gold (Imagine Dragons song)")".[\[66\]](#cite_note-66) "[Shots](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shots_\(Imagine_Dragons_song\) "Shots (Imagine Dragons song)")" was released as the album's third single on January 26, 2015.[\[67\]](#cite_note-67)

Imagine Dragons played at the [Mayan Theater](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mayan_Theater "Mayan Theater") in [Los Angeles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles "Los Angeles") on February 5, 2015. The half-hour set included the live debut of unreleased songs "Summer" and "[I'm So Sorry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I'm_So_Sorry "I'm So Sorry")".[\[68\]](#cite_note-68) On February 8, the band partnered with [Target](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Target_Corporation "Target Corporation") for a performance of "Shots" as part of a live commercial aired during the [Grammy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/57th_Annual_Grammy_Awards "57th Annual Grammy Awards"). _Smoke + Mirrors_ was released on February 17. The album debuted atop the Billboard 200, making it the band's first number one album. The band began a world tour in support of the album on June 3 in [Portland, Oregon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portland,_Oregon "Portland, Oregon").

During the band's tour, Imagine Dragons released two non-album singles. "[Roots](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roots_\(Imagine_Dragons_song\) "Roots (Imagine Dragons song)")" was released on August 26, 2015, and "[I Was Me](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Was_Me "I Was Me")" on October 12, 2015, via [iTunes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ITunes "ITunes"). The band also released a cover of "I Love You All the Time" by [Eagles of Death Metal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eagles_of_Death_Metal "Eagles of Death Metal") on December 18, 2015, in support of the victims of the [November 2015 Paris attacks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/November_2015_Paris_attacks "November 2015 Paris attacks"). The [Smoke + Mirrors Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smoke_+_Mirrors_Tour "Smoke + Mirrors Tour") ended on February 5, 2016, in [Amsterdam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amsterdam "Amsterdam"). The band released a one night only [concert film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Concert_film "Concert film"), _Imagine Dragons In Concert: Smoke + Mirrors_, in select theaters on March 2, 2016, which was later released on DVD and Blu-Ray.[\[69\]](#cite_note-69)

Following the tour, the band planned to take a hiatus. They released the soundtracks songs "[Not Today](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Not_Today_\(Imagine_Dragons_song\) "Not Today (Imagine Dragons song)")" from _[Me Before You](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Me_Before_You_\(soundtrack\) "Me Before You (soundtrack)")_ and "[Sucker for Pain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sucker_for_Pain "Sucker for Pain")" from _[Suicide Squad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suicide_Squad_\(soundtrack\) "Suicide Squad (soundtrack)")_ with [Lil Wayne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Wayne "Lil Wayne"), [Wiz Khalifa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wiz_Khalifa "Wiz Khalifa"), [Logic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Logic_\(rapper\) "Logic (rapper)"), [Ty Dolla Sign](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ty_Dolla_Sign "Ty Dolla Sign"), and [X Ambassadors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/X_Ambassadors "X Ambassadors") in April and June, respectively.[\[70\]](#cite_note-70)[\[71\]](#cite_note-71)

### 2016–2020: _Evolve_ and _Origins_

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/23/Imagine_Dragons_-_Uncasville_CT_-_November_2017_-_1.jpg/250px-Imagine_Dragons_-_Uncasville_CT_-_November_2017_-_1.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Imagine_Dragons_-_Uncasville_CT_-_November_2017_-_1.jpg)

Imagine Dragons performing at [Mohegan Sun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mohegan_Sun "Mohegan Sun") during the Evolve tour in November 2017.

Imagine Dragons began recording their third studio album in September 2016. The band teased the upcoming album by posting cryptic messages on their Twitter account for the next four months. They released the song "[Levitate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Levitate_\(Imagine_Dragons_song\) "Levitate (Imagine Dragons song)")", recorded for the film _[Passengers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Passengers_\(2016_film\) "Passengers (2016 film)")_, on December 2, 2016. On January 28, 2017, the band started posting a series of videos teasing the album's first single.[\[72\]](#cite_note-72) The time-lapse videos featured lead singer Dan Reynolds drawing surreal images on a drawing pad. [Morse code](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morse_code "Morse code") was hidden in the videos and translated to "objects of same color".\[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_\]

On February 1, 2017, Imagine Dragons released "[Believer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Believer_\(Imagine_Dragons_song\) "Believer (Imagine Dragons song)")" as the lead single for their next album. "Believer" was used as part of a [Super Bowl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl "Super Bowl") ad for the [Nintendo Switch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nintendo_Switch "Nintendo Switch").[\[73\]](#cite_note-73) On April
